facts.statement: Kelenken lived during the Middle Miocene epoch.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Middle Miocene (Colloncuran)~

facts.statement: The specimen was designated the holotype of the new species Kelenken guillermoi in 2007.
facts.quote: and was made the holotype of the new genus and species Kelenken guillermoi in 2007

facts.statement: The genus name Kelenken references a spirit from Tehuelche mythology.
facts.quote: The genus name references a spirit in Tehuelche mythology

facts.statement: Kelenken is the largest-known phorusrhacid, estimated to be 10% larger than its largest known relatives.
facts.quote: Kelenken is the largest-known phorusrhacid, 10% larger than its largest relatives known previously

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Kelenken is 716 mm long, making it the largest known bird skull.
facts.quote: At 716 mm long, the holotype skull is the largest known of any bird

facts.statement: The tarsometatarsus leg bone of Kelenken is 437 mm long.
facts.quote: The tarsometatarsus leg bone is 437 mm long

facts.statement: Kelenken is estimated to have stood about 3 meters tall and weighed over 100 kg.
facts.quote: Kelenken is thought to have been about 3 m tall and exceeded 100 kg in weight

facts.statement: Kelenken differed from other phorusrhacids by having a longer beak, a supraorbital ossification fitting into a postorbital socket, and an almost triangular foramen magnum.
facts.quote: Kelenken differed from other phorusrhacids in features such as the length of its beak, in having a supraorbital ossification (a rounded edge above the eye socket) that fits into a socket of the postorbital process, and in having an almost triangular foramen magnum

facts.statement: Kelenken belongs to the subfamily Phorusrhacinae, which includes Devincenzia.
facts.quote: Kelenken was found to belong in the subfamily Phorusrhacinae, along with for example Devincenzia

facts.statement: Kelenken is known from the Collón Curá Formation and lived during the Colloncuran age when open environments predominated.
facts.quote: Kelenken is known from the Collón Curá Formation, and lived during the Colloncuran age of South America, when open environments predominated

facts.statement: Fossils of a phorusrhacid were discovered around 2004 by Guillermo Aguirre-Zabala about 100 meters from the railroad in Comallo.
facts.quote: Around 2004, fossils of a phorusrhacid (or "terror bird", a group of large, predatory birds) were discovered by Argentine high school student Guillermo Aguirre-Zabala between two houses, about 100 m from the railroad of Comallo

facts.statement: The specimen is cataloged as BAR 3877-11 in the collection of the Museo Asociación Paleontológica Bariloche.
facts.quote: The specimen became part of the collection of the Museo Asociación Paleontológica Bariloche in Río Negro, where it was cataloged as specimen BAR 3877-11

facts.statement: The specimen was reported and discussed by Luis M. Chiappe and Sara Bertelli in a 2006 article before receiving a scientific name.
facts.quote: Prior to the animal receiving a scientific name, the specimen was reported and discussed by the Argentine paleontologists Luis M. Chiappe and Sara Bertelli in a short 2006 article

facts.statement: Bertelli, Chiappe, and Claudia Tambussi designated the specimen as the holotype of Kelenken guillermoi in 2007.
facts.quote: In 2007, Bertelli, Chiappe, and Claudia Tambussi made the specimen the holotype of Kelenken guillermoi

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a nearly complete skull that is somewhat crushed, preserving most eye sockets, the skull roof, braincase, and left quadrate bone.
facts.quote: The holotype and only known specimen consists of a nearly complete skull which is somewhat crushed from top to bottom, with most of the eye sockets, skull roof, braincase and left quadrate bone preserved

facts.statement: The specimen includes a left tarsometatarsus, a partial foot phalanx, and some indeterminate fragments.
facts.quote: The specimen also includes an associated left tarsometatarsus (lower leg bone of birds), a small upper portion of a foot phalanx bone (toe bone), and some indeterminate fragments

facts.statement: Bertelli and colleagues classified Kelenken as a member of the family Phorusrhacidae in 2007.
facts.quote: In their 2007 description, Bertelli and colleagues classified Kelenken as a member of the family Phorusrhacidae

facts.statement: A 2011 phylogenetic analysis found Kelenken and Devincenzia to be sister taxa.
facts.quote: The Brazilian paleontologist Herculano Alvarenga and colleagues published a phylogenetic analysis of Phorusrhacidae in 2011 that found Kelenken and Devincenzia to be sister taxa, each other's closest relatives

facts.statement: A 2015 analysis found the subfamily Phorusrhacinae to be polyphyletic.
facts.quote: In their 2015 description of Llallawavis, the Argentinian paleontologist Federico J. Degrange and colleagues performed a phylogenetic analysis of Phorusrhacidae, wherein they found Phorusrhacinae to be polyphyletic (an unnatural grouping)

facts.statement: Phorusrhacids are an extinct group within Cariamiformes, whose only living members are seriemas.
facts.quote: Phorusrhacids are an extinct group within Cariamiformes, the only living members of which are the two species of seriemas in the family Cariamidae

facts.statement: Phorusrhacids were present in South America from the Paleocene until the Pleistocene.
facts.quote: Phorusrhacids were present in South America from the Paleocene (when the continent was an isolated island) and survived until the Pleistocene

facts.statement: It is unclear whether phorusrhacids originated in South America or arrived from elsewhere when continents were closer or sea levels were lower.
facts.quote: It is unclear where the group originated; both cariamids and phorusrhacids may have arisen in South America, or arrived from elsewhere when southern continents were closer together or when sea levels were lower

facts.statement: Kelenken lived during the middle Miocene, approximately 15 million years ago.
facts.quote: Kelenken itself lived during the middle Miocene, about 15 million years ago

facts.statement: The classification of European fossils assigned to phorusrhacids is disputed.
facts.quote: while fossils from Europe have been assigned to the group, their classification is disputed

facts.statement: Kelenken is the largest known phorusrhacid, approximately 10% larger than previously known large species like Phorusrhacos.
facts.quote: Kelenken is the largest known phorusrhacid, about 10% larger than the largest phorusrhacids previously known, such as Phorusrhacos.

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Kelenken measures about 716 mm in length from the beak tip to the nuchal crest.
facts.quote: The holotype skull is about 716 mm long from the tip of the beak to the center of the sagittal nuchal crest at the upper back of the head

facts.statement: The hind end of the Kelenken skull is 312 mm wide.
facts.quote: The hind end of the skull is 312 mm wide.

facts.statement: The head height of Kelenken reached up to 3 meters, compared to 90 cm for modern seriemas.
facts.quote: The head height was up to 3 m, while modern seriemas reach 90 cm in height.

facts.statement: Although not specifically estimated, Kelenken is thought to have weighed more than 100 kg.
facts.quote: While the weight of Kelenken has not been specifically estimated, it is thought to have exceeded 100 kg.

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Kelenken is very massive, triangular from above, and compressed from top to bottom at the hind portion.
facts.quote: The holotype skull is very massive, and triangular when viewed from above, with the hind portion compressed from top to bottom.

facts.statement: The upper beak of Kelenken exceeds half the skull's total length and is longer than that of Phorusrhacos, unlike in Mesembriornis and Patagornis.
facts.quote: The upper beak is very long, exceeding half the total length of the skull, unlike in Mesembriornis and Patagornis, and is longer than that of Phorusrhacos.

facts.statement: The front end of the premaxilla in Kelenken projects as a sharp, downturned hook.
facts.quote: The front end of the premaxilla (the frontmost bone of the upper jaw) prominently projects as a sharp, downturned hook.

facts.statement: The underside of the front portion of Kelenken's upper beak features prominent ridges separated by grooves from the sharp edge.
facts.quote: The underside of the upper beak's front portion forms a pair of prominent ridges that are each separated by a groove from the tomium, or sharp edge of the beak.

facts.statement: The antorbital fenestra in Kelenken retains a clear quadrangular shape despite some crushing on both sides.
facts.quote: The quadrangular shape of the antorbital fenestra (an opening in front of the eye socket) is clear despite it being crushed somewhat on both sides.

facts.statement: The jugal bone of Kelenken is about four times taller than thick at the lower center of the eye socket and is taller than in other phorusrhacids.
facts.quote: The jugal bone is about four times taller than thick by the lower center of the eyesocket, and its height is greater than in other phorusrhacids.

facts.statement: The occipital table of Kelenken is very wide and low, giving it a rectangular appearance from behind, similar to Devicenzia.
facts.quote: The occipital table is very wide, like in Devicenzia, and low, which gives it a rectangular appearance when viewed from behind.

facts.statement: The foramen magnum of Kelenken is almost triangular, a unique feature for this genus.
facts.quote: The foramen magnum (the large opening at the base of the skull through which the spinal cord enters) is almost triangular, uniquely for this genus

facts.statement: Researchers Alvarenga and Elizabeth Höfling published general remarks on phorusrhacid habits in a 2003 article.
facts.quote: Alvarenga and Elizabeth Höfling made some general remarks about phorusrhacid habits in a 2003 article.

facts.statement: Large lacrimal bone expansions above the eyes suggest phorusrhacids hunted by sight in open, sunlit areas rather than shaded forests.
facts.quote: The large expansions above the eyes formed by the lacrimal bones (similar to what is seen in modern hawks) would have protected the eyes against the sun, and enabled keen eyesight, which indicates they hunted by sight in open, sunlit areas, and not shaded forests.

facts.statement: Chiappe and Bertelli argued in 2006 that the discovery of Kelenken challenged the idea that larger phorusrhacids were less agile than smaller ones.
facts.quote: According to Chiappe and Bertelli in 2006, the discovery of Kelenken shed doubt on the traditional idea that the size and agility of phorusrhacids correlated, with the larger members of the group being more bulky and less adapted for running.

facts.statement: Chiappe stated in 2006 that Kelenken could run faster than previously assumed for large phorusrhacids, despite not being as swift as an ostrich.
facts.quote: In a 2006 news article about the discovery, Chiappe stated that while Kelenken may not have been as swift as an ostrich, it could clearly run faster than had previously been assumed for large phorusrhacids, based on the long, slender leg-bones, superficially similar to those of the modern, flightless rhea.

facts.statement: John J. Flynn commented in 2006 that other large South American predators were less numerous and agile than phorusrhacids, which had ample grazing mammal prey.
facts.quote: In another 2006 news article about the find, the American paleontologist John J. Flynn commented that while there were other large predators in South America at the time, they were limited in numbers and not as fast and agile as the phorusrhacids, and the many grazing mammals would have provided ample prey.

facts.statement: Degrange and colleagues conducted a 2010 study using Finite Element Analysis and CT scans to estimate the bite force and stress distribution of the phorusrhacid Andalgalornis.
facts.quote: A 2010 study by Degrange and colleagues of the medium-sized phorusrhacid Andalgalornis, based on Finite Element Analysis using CT scans, estimated its bite force and stress distribution in its skull.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested Andalgalornis either fed on small prey swallowed whole or used an "attack-and-retreat" strategy with repetitive beak strikes for large prey.
facts.quote: Instead, they suggested that it either fed on smaller prey that could be killed and consumed more safely, by for example swallowing it whole, or that when targeting large prey, it used a series of well-targeted repetitive strikes with the beak, in an "attack-and-retreat" strategy.

facts.statement: Tambussi and colleagues analyzed the neck flexibility of Andalgalornis in a 2012 study, finding its neck divided into three sections.
facts.quote: A 2012 follow-up study by Tambussi and colleagues analyzed the flexibility of the neck of Andalgalornis, based on the morphology of its neck vertebrae, finding the neck to be divided into three sections.

facts.statement: Tambussi and colleagues assumed that the neck adaptations of Andalgalornis for carrying a large head and rising after a strike were also true for other large phorusrhacids.
facts.quote: By manually manipulating the vertebrae, they concluded that the neck musculature and skeleton of Andalgalornis was adapted to carrying a large head, and for helping it rise from a maximum extension after a downwards strike, and the researchers assumed the same would be true for other large, big-headed phorusrhacids.

facts.statement: Degrange found in a 2020 study that phorusrhacids evolved from a seriema-like ancestor into two main skull morphotypes.
facts.quote: A 2020 study of phorusrhacid skull morphology by Degrange found that there were two main morphotypes within the group, derived from a seriema-like ancestor.

facts.statement: The "Terror Bird Skull Type" included Kelenken and other large members and was more specialized with rigid skulls compared to the plesiomorphic "Psilopterine Skull Type".
facts.quote: These were the "Psilopterine Skull Type", which was plesiomorphic (more similar to the ancestral type), and the "Terror Bird Skull Type", which included Kelenken and other large members, that was more specialized, with more rigid and stiff skulls.

facts.statement: Studies show that both phorusrhacid skull types handled prey similarly, but the rigid "Terror Bird" skulls were adapted for handling larger prey.
facts.quote: Despite the differences, studies have shown the two types handled prey similarly, while the more rigid skulls and resulting larger bite force of the "Terror Bird" type would have been an adaptation to handling larger prey.

facts.statement: Kelenken fossils were found in pyroclastic outcrops of the Collón Curá Formation near Comallo in Patagonia.
facts.quote: Kelenken was discovered in pyroclastic (rocks ejected by volcanic eruptions) outcrops belonging to the Collón Curá Formation in the southeastern corner of Comallo, Patagonia

facts.statement: The age of the sediments containing Kelenken is estimated to be about 15 million years old, corresponding to the middle Miocene.
facts.quote: it is estimated to date to the Colloncuran age of the middle Miocene, about 15 million years ago

facts.statement: Kelenken lived in open, semi-arid to temperate woodlands or bushlands with reduced plant cover.
facts.quote: The Collón Curá Formation and the Colloncuran age of South America represent a time when more open environments with reduced plant covering predominated, similar to semi-arid and temperate to warm, dry woodlands or bushlands

facts.statement: The open environment of the time favored large, cursorial animals like Kelenken.
facts.quote: The open environment allowed more cursorial (adapted for running) and large animals to occur

facts.statement: Kelenken belongs to the family Phorusrhacidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Phorusrhacidae

facts.statement: The time range for Kelenken is estimated from 15.5 to 13.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Langhian to Serravallian (15.5 to 13.8 million years ago)
